messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.

Our team needs a rocket design. We need at least 10,000 feet, and it has to land within 5 minutes of liftoff so it doesn't drift off the field. Use dual deployment. Wind is usually around 12 mph. Provide the design and expected performance.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: Apogee at least 10,000 ft. 10,000 * 0.3048 = 3,048 m, a floor. The flight has to be back on the ground within 5 minutes of liftoff, so total flight time is at most 300 s. Dual deployment. Wind is around 12 mph. 12 * 0.447 = 5.36 m/s, and that wind goes in every simulation. Rail and site are not stated: 1.5 m vertical rail, sea level. Landing speed is not stated, so the 6 m/s gate applies to the main.

2. Feasibility: 300 s is the tight constraint. Ascent to 3,048 m is on the order of 20 s, which leaves about 280 s to come down. A single chute at under 6 m/s would take 3,048 / 6 = 508 s and would miss the clock. Dual deploy with a fast drogue is required. The motor has to clear 3,048 m without a huge coast that eats the clock. Looking up a K that can do that in a short dual-deploy airframe.

2. Feasibility: The lookup resolves K1200 to a Cesaroni 2014K1200-16A: 2008 N*s, 1189 N average, burn 1.69 s, diameter 0.054 m, length 0.404 m, mass 1.63 kg. The only delay is 16 s, a single ejection, so the motor flies plugged and an altimeter does the dual deploy. A 60 mm tube fits the motor and two chutes. A single chute would take 3,048 / 6 = 508 s, past the 300 s clock.

3. Size: Liftoff guess 2.6 kg. Thrust-to-weight is 1189 / (2.6 * 9.81) = 46.6. Weight is 2.6 * 9.81 = 25.5 N, rail acceleration (1189 - 25.5) / 2.6 = 448 m/s^2, exit speed sqrt(2 * 448 * 1.5) = 36.7 m/s. Drogue for about 1.8 kg at 22 m/s: area 2 * 1.8 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 484) = 0.074 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.074 / pi) = 0.31 m. I will fly 0.40 m so it is still a canopy but the descent stays fast. Main for about 1.7 kg at 5 m/s: area 2 * 1.7 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 25) = 1.36 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 1.36 / pi) = 1.32 m. I will fly 1.6 m, opening at 200 m, so the slow part is short enough to finish inside 300 s.

4. Draft: 60 mm fiberglass, tube 1.00 m, ogive nose, four fiberglass fins, Cesaroni K1200 plugged, 0.04 kg altimeter, 0.40 m drogue at apogee, 1.6 m main at 200 m. Wind 5.36 m/s, 1.5 m rail.
